metadata.Name: MultiWOZ-X
metadata.Description: MultiWOZ-X is a large-scale multilingual dataset for task-oriented dialog (TOD). It contains 2,000 human-written dialogs from MultiWOZ 2.1, translated and re-annotated by professional translators into Arabic, Chinese, German, and Russian, enabling evaluation of cross-lingual transfer for tasks like Dialog State Tracking and Response Retrieval.
metadata.Paper Title: MultiWOZ-X: A Large-Scale Multilingual Cross-Lingual Task-Oriented Dialogue Dataset
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
metadata.Abstract: Current research in task-oriented dialog (TOD) is severely limited by the lack of multilingual datasets. This has two main negative effects: 1) it prevents the development of truly multilingual TOD systems, and 2) it makes it impossible to reliably evaluate the cross-lingual transfer capabilities of state-of-the-art pretrained language models (PrLMs) for TOD tasks. In this work, we introduce MultiWOZ-X, the first large-scale multilingual dataset for cross-lingual and multilingual fine-tuning and evaluation in TOD. It is a collection of 2,000 human-written dialogs from the original English MultiWOZ 2.1, translated and re-annotated by professional translators into 4 new languages: Arabic, Chinese, German, and Russian. We provide a thorough analysis of the new dataset and its properties. We then establish a series of strong baselines for two main TOD tasks, Dialog State Tracking (DST) and Response Retrieval (RR), in two cross-lingual transfer setups: zero-shot and few-shot. Our results indicate that 1) conversational pretraining on target languages is crucial for effective cross-lingual transfer, and 2) few-shot learning with only a handful of target-language dialogs is a viable and data-efficient alternative to full-scale data collection and annotation in new languages. We release the new dataset and the code to the public.
